newsitem.title: INDONESIA: U.N. East Timor envoy due in Jakarta on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: U.N. East Timor envoy due in Jakarta on Thursday.

text.p: The U.N. special envoy for East Timor, Jamsheed Marker, was due in Indonesia on Thursday on what diplomatic sources said was a familiarisation trip following his appointment in February.
"This is very much a familiarisation visit," one diplomat said. "He has been saying he will decide how to take the issue forward after visiting Lisbon, Jakarta and East Timor."

Diplomatic sources said Marker, 74, would arrive on Thursday morning, and was to see Foreign Minister Ali Alatas before going to East Timor on Saturday. He was to return to Jakarta next Monday and would probably leave Indonesia around March 28.

U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan appointed Marker, a former Pakistani ambassador to the United Nations, as his special representative in a bid to move forward U.N.-sponsored talks between Portugal and Indonesia to find an internationally acceptable solution to the East Timor issue.
Indonesia invaded the territory on December 7, 1975, after civil war began on the tropical island following the withdrawal of Portuguese colonial authorities four months earlier.
Indonesia absorbed the territory as its 27th province the next July in a move the United Nations has not recognised.
Foreign Minister Alatas has said Indonesia welcomed moves by Annan to give new impetus to talks that have dragged on for almost 15 years with resolution.
Marker visited Portugal earlier this month and said in Lisbon that he was hopeful of speeding up negotiations between Portugal and Indonesia.
"I continue to be optimistic...the negotiations are going to continue," he said after meeting Portuguese Foreign Minister Jaime Gama.

East Timorese independence activist Jose Ramos Horta, who shared the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize with East Timor's Roman Catholic Bishop Carlos Belo, met Annan at the United Nations on March 11 -- the first meeting between Horta and a U.N. chief.
Horta told reporters after the meeting that Indonesia's President Suharto was the only impediment to change in East Timor.
